summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data (3995 CGM readings, 98.7 percent coverage, 5 minute cadence, no invalid or duplicate readings) show an overall average of 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, time above range 8.9 percent, time below range 5.1 percent, and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent. The overnight and early morning window (04:00 to 08:00 local) is the most stable part of the day with 95 to 98 percent time in range. Two recurring problem windows dominate: a broad afternoon elevation peaking at 16:00 local (average 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range) and a clustered low burden in the early evening (19:00 local, 15.3 percent below range) and late evening into early night (23:00 to 03:00 local, 10 to 18.5 percent below range). Treatment telemetry contains 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U but zero carbohydrate entries, and carbohydrates on board were zero in every supplied loop status, so unannounced-meal detection is the entire meal response. Loop statuses show a strongly bend-dependent effective sensitivity ranging from about 124 mg/dL/U at low glucose to about 27.8 mg/dL/U at high glucose against a flat profile insulin sensitivity factor of 56 mg/dL/U, with peak insulin on board of 5.935 U while carbohydrates on board were zero. The recurring sequence in the response windows is: unannounced rise, late and strong correction, level 2 low, apparent unlogged rescue carbohydrate, rebound. The configuration ceilings (maximum insulin on board 25 U, maximum basal 12 U/h) are far above anything the system actually used and therefore place no practical bound on this sequence.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data are sufficient for hourly and daily pattern analysis: 3995 valid entries, 0 invalid, 0 duplicate, 0 out of period, estimated cadence 5.0 minutes, coverage 98.7 percent of 4046 expected readings, 10 gaps with a largest gap of 65 minutes. The period runs 2026-08-07 21:14 to 2026-08-21 21:14 UTC; the first day (33 readings) and last day (269 readings) are partial and were down-weighted in day-level comparisons. Local timezone is BST at plus 60 minutes and hourly_glucose_local is a clean plus one hour shift of hourly_glucose, confirmed by matching values, so all time-of-day statements use local hours. The AAPS profile is complete: 7 basal segments, 5 carb ratio segments, 1 flat insulin sensitivity segment, 3 target segments, duration of insulin action, and a full settings block; profile_context marks aaps_profile as authoritative with historical_applicability yes. Telemetry is heavily sampled down: only 40 of 2315 treatments, 24 of 6214 device statuses and 24 therapy response windows are included, so no continuous insulin on board or delivered basal series exists. Carbohydrate telemetry is entirely absent (0 carb entries, 0.0 total grams, empty carb_treatment_entries). Confounders inside the window: AAPS restarts on 08-09, infusion site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, a profile switch to a flat sensitivity profile on 08-13, GLP-1 1.25 mg doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20, an occlusion plus pump error on 08-19, and several temporary targets of 135 mg/dL. Loop reason strings contain non-standard constructs (UAM Boost, Enhanced oref1, twin, antBackout, prTrial arms), indicating an AAPS variant rather than stock oref1.

analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycaemia is the leading safety signal and it is clustered rather than diffuse. Time below range is 5.1 percent overall, above the 4 percent convention, while coefficient of variation 32.6 percent is below the 36 percent threshold. Local hours above 10 percent below range: 01:00 at 18.5, 19:00 at 15.3, 00:00 at 11.4, 03:00 at 10.2, 02:00 at 10.1, 23:00 at 10.1. Level 2 lows appear in glucose_extremes on 08-13 around 18:00 to 18:15 local (51, 47, 42, 45), on 08-14 around 19:05 to 19:15 local (48, 41, 41) and on 08-21 at 07:19 local (42). Eight of the fourteen full days had a minimum at or below 56 mg/dL. Highs reach 285 to 293 mg/dL on 08-15 late afternoon and 08-18 midday. Large loop-driven falls are documented: 234 to 56 within 120 minutes on 08-14, 264 to 96 within 120 minutes on 08-19 with insulin on board 4.73 U, 206 to 53 within 180 minutes on 08-16, and 172 to 47 within 240 minutes on 08-13. At report generation the system was at 245 mg/dL rising with 5.935 U insulin on board, zero carbohydrates on board, effective sensitivity 27.8 mg/dL/U and a requested 4 U/h temporary basal, which is the same precondition that preceded the documented overshoots. The two worst days are 08-14 (time in range 70.8 percent) and 08-18 (time below range 12.8 percent), both adjacent to GLP-1 dosing and infusion set changes, and 08-19 is confounded by the recorded occlusion and pump error. Safety ceilings are effectively absent: maximum insulin on board 25 U exceeds a full day of total insulin use, and maximum basal 12 U/h is roughly fifteen times the highest scheduled basal of 0.8 U/h.

analysis_steps.findings: The scheduled basal totals 16.2 U per day across 7 segments, consistent with the profile switch note describing roughly 16.2 U per day. The most fasting-like window, 04:00 to 08:00 local, shows averages of 99 to 110 mg/dL, time in range 95 to 98 percent and time below range 1.3 to 4.8 percent under basal rates of 0.6 to 0.8 U/h, which is the strongest available evidence that overall basal magnitude is not grossly wrong. An apparent phase mismatch exists on paper: basal peaks at 0.8 U/h from 06:00 while glucose is flattest, falls to its minimum of 0.5 U/h at 16:00 exactly at the glycaemic peak of 162.8 mg/dL, and steps back up at 18:00 and 19:00 into the window with the highest daytime low burden. However this mismatch cannot be converted into a basal defect, because at least four explanations remain unseparated for the 10:00 to 17:00 elevation: unannounced meals handled only by unannounced-meal detection with its inherent detection lag, genuinely insufficient basal, GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying shifting absorption later, and infusion set ageing plus the documented occlusion. The meal-shaped onset at 09:00 to 10:00 and again at 12:00, together with 0 percent below range and only 1.8 percent above range at 08:00, favours the unannounced-meal explanation. For the 18:00 to 20:00 lows, the correction-tail explanation is better supported than the basal step, because the lows follow documented large-drop episodes on 08-13, 08-14 and 08-16 rather than occurring on quiet days. The 23:00 to 03:00 decline self-corrects from 04:00 under an unchanged or higher basal rate, which argues against excessive overnight basal and for a residual insulin tail. Targets cannot be evaluated as delivered: the profile declares 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL, but loop statuses show effective targets of 80, 84, 86, 87, 90, 96.4, 99, 101, 104, 105, 106, 108 and 116 mg/dL, including values below the declared floor when no temporary target was active. Recurrent 135 mg/dL temporary targets on 08-09, 08-17, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-20 add a further confounder because they suppress microbolusing under the current activation settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratio is unverifiable in this package. All five segments (13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5 and 12.6 g/U) are present and are echoed inside loop reason strings, confirming they are loaded, but with zero carbohydrate entries no bolus was ever computed from them, so they influence dosing only indirectly through the dynamic sensitivity path. This is a blocked assessment, not a defect. The insulin sensitivity factor is a single flat segment of 56 mg/dL/U, but the delivered sensitivity is not that value: with dynamic sensitivity enabled at an adjustment factor of 70 percent, the observed variable sensitivity spans 124.0, 111.9 and 108.4 mg/dL/U at glucose of 69.8, 95.1 and 84 mg/dL, roughly 68 to 90 mg/dL/U in the 95 to 140 range, and 42.5, 43.2, 39.99, 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U at glucose from 135 to 246 mg/dL. The delivered response is therefore about half as strong as the profile value in the normal range and about twice as strong at high glucose. This non-linearity is the most economical single explanation for the observed sawtooth: a slow response while glucose climbs through the late morning and afternoon, then a very strong burst once glucose is high (insulin requirement 1.45 to 2.59 U, temporary basals of 3.2 to 4 U/h, insulin on board reaching 4.7 to 5.9 U with zero carbohydrates on board), then the two-hour falls of 168 and 178 mg/dL and the evening and night low clusters. It directly competes with the basal phase-mismatch reading, and the two are not separable without announced meals. Duration of insulin action is 10 hours with a free peak insulin model. Consistent with a long tail, very small evening corrections are followed by disproportionate multi-hour declines: 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL falling to 68 at 180 minutes and 57 at 240 minutes on 08-17, 0.15 U at 138 falling to 82 to 87 on 08-12, and 0.05 U at 93 falling to 69 on 08-10. Whether 10 hours is over-long or is intended for the free peak model cannot be decided from CGM data alone, and it interacts with the ceiling settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Microbolusing and unannounced-meal detection are both enabled and mutually consistent. Because carbohydrate entries are zero and carbohydrates on board were zero in all supplied loop statuses, unannounced-meal detection is not an assist layer but the entire meal-response system; there is no duplicate carbohydrate counting, since unannounced-meal deviations are the only input. The reactive nature of this arrangement is visible on 08-18, where a deviation of 2.3 and a delta of 4.83 led to an eventual glucose of 222 mg/dL, an insulin requirement of 1.45 U and an enacted 3.2 U/h. Among activation conditions, always-enabled microbolusing supersedes the with-carbohydrates and after-carbohydrates switches, which are therefore inert labels rather than active restrictions; this is a cosmetic inconsistency only. The materially active condition is that microbolusing is disabled during high temporary targets, which suppressed microbolusing during the recurring 135 mg/dL temporary targets on 08-17, 08-18 and 08-19, all in the afternoon and overlapping the highest above-range hours. That setting is nevertheless hypo-protective and works in the same direction as the dominant safety constraint, so it is retained. Within delivery limits, the maximum unannounced-meal microbolus size of 20 basal minutes exceeds the standard maximum of 15 basal minutes, and because carbohydrates are never announced, the larger and more speculative cap is the only one that ever applies; this points the wrong way given the 15.3 percent below range at 19:00 local. The microbolus interval of 3 minutes is not the binding rate limiter, because CGM cadence is 5.0 minutes and loop cycles follow the CGM, so changing it would have little effect. An important limiting observation: the variant delivers more than the configured standard bolus cap in at least two documented cycles, microbolusing 0.4 U against a standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U on 08-07 and delivering a 1.6 U microbolus under a high boost on 08-19, so tightening the unannounced-meal cap may have a smaller effect than the nominal setting suggests.

analysis_steps.findings: Maximum basal of 12 U/h is non-binding and inert: the practical ceiling is visible in the loop text where an adjusted requested rate of 5.9 U/h was limited to a maximum safe basal of 4 U/h on 08-14, consistent with the daily safety multiplier of 5 applied to the 0.8 U/h peak basal. Aligning the configured maximum basal to the already effective ceiling would be behaviourally neutral while restoring a meaningful bound. Maximum insulin on board of 25 U is the single largest unguarded exposure in the configuration: logged insulin is 275.95 U over 14 days, roughly 19.7 U per day, and the scheduled basal is 16.2 U per day, so the ceiling exceeds a full day of insulin. The highest observed insulin on board was 5.935 U with zero carbohydrates on board at 245 mg/dL on 08-21, and 4.73 U with zero carbohydrates on board at 262 mg/dL on 08-19. Because nothing in fourteen days approached even 8 U, tightening the ceiling would not alter normal dosing while truncating exactly the excursions documented on 08-14, 08-16 and 08-19. On sensitivity, the configuration is internally coherent: Autosens disabled with dynamic sensitivity enabled is one sensitivity path rather than two, and with Autosens off the target adjustment flags are correctly inert. A sensitivity ratio of 1, present in most supplied statuses, is a neutral current adjustment and is not evidence of anything disabled; the non-neutral values of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 appear on hypo-guard cycles and are consistent with the dynamic path operating normally. The dynamic sensitivity adjustment factor of 70 percent is the largest single therapeutic lever, but it is bidirectionally conflicted: lowering it would weaken the high-glucose over-correction and help the low burden, yet it would simultaneously weaken the already slow response in the 100 to 150 range and worsen the afternoon elevation. It is also coupled to the flat profile sensitivity value and to the boost behaviour, so three inputs feed one observed outcome and none can be attributed without sequential testing. As a safety observation outside the decision inventory, the maximum daily safety multiplier of 5.0 and the current basal safety multiplier of 6.0 both exceed common defaults and are the reason the effective ceiling is 4 U/h rather than a lower value; combined with the 25 U insulin on board ceiling, the whole safety envelope is widened at once.

analysis_steps.findings: The user-declared analysis context is present and carries a declaration timestamp of 2026-08-21T21:08:10Z with source declared_by_user, and within it meal_strategies is an empty list, period_exceptions is null and strategy_stable_for_period is null. Because no prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage or extended carbohydrate fields were declared at all, there is no declared value to compare against execution, and no representative period-wide declaration can be assumed; applicability and confidence are limited accordingly. Declared context and telemetry agree rather than conflict: an empty declaration matches zero logged carbohydrates. All 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses of 0.05 to 2.4 U with a median near 0.2 U, and all have the extended carbohydrate flag false. Three recurring shapes appear. First, unannounced meals answered only after the fact: 0.2 U at 100 mg/dL rising to 235 at 240 minutes on 08-14, 0.05 U at 164 with 186 still present at 360 minutes on 08-19, and 0.35 U at 189 rising to 206 at 120 minutes on 08-21. Second, high-glucose correction followed by a level 2 low and then a rebound: 172 to 47 at 240 minutes and then 204 at 360 minutes on 08-13, 234 to 56 at 120 minutes on 08-14, and 206 to 53 at 180 minutes then 158 at 240 minutes on 08-16. Rebounds of 80 to 157 mg/dL within 60 to 120 minutes of a level 2 low cannot be produced by insulin dynamics or basal, and the most consistent explanation is unlogged rescue carbohydrate, which the loop must then re-detect as a fresh unannounced rise. Third, small evening corrections with disproportionate tails, where 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL preceded a fall to 57 at 240 minutes on 08-17; a 0.05 U bolus cannot cause a 68 mg/dL fall, so this reflects the long duration of insulin action tail of earlier microboluses plus the weak normal-range end of the dynamic sensitivity curve. Meal timing can be inferred as a pattern only, not as composition: rises at 09:00 to 10:00, at 12:00 to 14:00, and a broad plateau peaking at 16:00 local, with the fall into 18:00 and 19:00 where the low burden concentrates. GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 at a roughly three-day cadence are a genuine confounder for any timing conclusion.

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carbohydrate assessment is possible. Extended carbohydrate entries are zero, the average extended carbohydrate duration field is null, the extended carbohydrate flag is false in all 24 therapy response windows, and carb_treatment_entries is an empty list. No amount, start offset, duration or observed action time exists and none is inferred; in particular no duration is derived from any aggregate average. Extended carbohydrates are a carbohydrate-entry construct and are not equivalent to a pump extended bolus, so their absence means the carbohydrate-modelling path was never used, which is distinct from how insulin was actually delivered. Consequently the carbohydrate absorption group, comprising a minimum five-minute carbohydrate impact of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and a maximum meal absorption of 7 hours, was inert throughout the period and has no observational basis for tuning; it shows no inconsistency and both values are conventional. One indirect signal is held as a hypothesis only: the 14:00 to 17:00 plateau is broad and slow-resolving rather than a sharp spike and coincides with GLP-1 dosing, which is the shape extended carbohydrates are designed for, but this requires meal-linked evidence before it could support any configuration.

analysis_steps.findings: Contradiction audit performed against aaps_profile, profile_context and decision_inventory. Corrections applied to earlier checkpoints: the earlier reading of sensitivity ratio values as evidence of a hidden mechanism running despite Autosens being off is withdrawn, because a ratio of 1 is a neutral adjustment and the observed values are consistent with the enabled dynamic sensitivity path; unannounced-meal detection is not treated as duplicate carbohydrate counting, since carbohydrates on board were zero throughout; the microbolus interval is taken only from the configuration field and no inference is drawn from remaining-time text in reason strings; the basal phase-mismatch hypothesis is demoted from a probable defect to a secondary observation because the 04:00 to 08:00 window performs well under the same schedule and because meal, correction and absorption explanations remain unresolved; and the declared empty meal strategy is treated as a present declaration containing no values, not as missing data. All six AAPS groups have non-null components, so verify is unavailable and every AAPS decision is change or keep. Competing explanations for the afternoon elevation are unannounced-meal detection lag, insufficient afternoon basal, GLP-1 delayed absorption, microbolus suppression during high temporary targets, and infusion set issues; the evidence does not separate them, so no basal, carb ratio, sensitivity, target or duration value is changed in this round. Competing explanations for the evening and night lows are the correction tail from the strong high-glucose response, the basal step at 18:00 and 19:00, and unlogged rescue carbohydrate rebound cycles; the correction tail is best supported. The only actions supported by evidence that do not depend on resolving those competitions are the two ceiling settings, because nothing in fourteen days approached them and tightening them therefore does not alter normal dosing while bounding the documented worst case. The maximum unannounced-meal microbolus size is a secondary candidate, deferred to a separate round because it does change routine delivery and because the boost behaviour makes its effect size uncertain. The single highest-value non-insulin action is starting to log carbohydrates for one recurring meal, which converts carb ratio, the absorption model and detection lag from untestable to testable.

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent and not a limiting factor: 98.7 percent coverage, a stable 5.0 minute cadence, zero invalid, zero duplicate and zero out-of-period readings, with a largest gap of only 65 minutes over fourteen days.

Overall glycaemic control is good by consensus metrics: time in range 86.0 percent, average glucose 121.6 mg/dL and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, which is below the 36 percent variability threshold.

The overnight and early morning window is stable and well matched by the current basal schedule, with 04:00 to 08:00 local showing 95 to 98 percent time in range and only 1.3 to 4.8 percent time below range under 0.6 to 0.8 U/h.

The AAPS profile is complete and internally coherent: all 7 basal, 5 carb ratio, 1 sensitivity and 3 target segments are populated, and the sensitivity configuration uses a single path with Autosens off and dynamic sensitivity on rather than two competing mechanisms.

Event logging of context is good: infusion site changes, sensor changes, profile switches, GLP-1 doses and an occlusion with pump error are all recorded, which made it possible to identify and set aside confounded days rather than misattribute them to profile settings.
The loop demonstrably respects its internal safety limit, capping an adjusted request of 5.9 U/h at the 4 U/h maximum safe basal on 08-14.

Several days show excellent results under the same configuration, including 95.5 to 97.0 percent time in range on 08-08 and 08-09, indicating the underlying profile is workable rather than fundamentally wrong.

issues.title: Clustered hypoglycaemia in the early evening and late evening into early night
issues.detail: Overall time below range is 5.1 percent, above the 4 percent convention, and it is concentrated rather than spread out: 19:00 local at 15.3 percent, 01:00 at 18.5 percent, 00:00 at 11.4 percent, 03:00 at 10.2 percent, 02:00 at 10.1 percent and 23:00 at 10.1 percent. Level 2 lows are documented on 08-13 (down to 42 mg/dL around 18:00 local), 08-14 (41 mg/dL around 19:10 local) and 08-21 (42 mg/dL at 07:19 local), and eight of fourteen full days had a minimum at or below 56 mg/dL.

issues.title: No effective ceiling on insulin on board
issues.detail: The maximum insulin on board limit of 25 U exceeds a full day of total insulin use, given 275.95 U over fourteen days and a 16.2 U per day scheduled basal. Observed peaks reached 5.935 U with zero carbohydrates on board at 245 mg/dL and 4.73 U with zero carbohydrates on board at 262 mg/dL, and the configured limit provides no practical bound before such accumulation becomes clinically relevant. The maximum basal setting of 12 U/h is likewise inert, since the effective ceiling resolved to 4 U/h.

issues.title: Repeating cycle of late strong correction, level 2 low and rebound
issues.detail: The therapy response windows show 234 to 56 mg/dL within 120 minutes on 08-14, 264 to 96 within 120 minutes on 08-19 with 4.73 U of insulin on board, 206 to 53 within 180 minutes on 08-16, and 172 to 47 within 240 minutes followed by 204 at 360 minutes on 08-13. Rebounds of 80 to 157 mg/dL within 60 to 120 minutes of a level 2 low cannot be produced by insulin dynamics, which points to rescue carbohydrate that is not logged and is therefore re-detected by the system as a new unannounced rise.

issues.title: Broad afternoon elevation peaking at 16:00 local
issues.detail: Local hourly averages rise from 132.9 mg/dL at 09:00 to 148.0 at 10:00 and reach 162.8 at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range and 0.0 percent below range, with 14:00 at 26.3 percent and 15:00 at 23.6 percent above range. At least four explanations remain unseparated: unannounced-meal detection lag, an afternoon basal trough of 0.5 U/h from 16:00, GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying, and microbolus suppression during the recurring 135 mg/dL temporary targets.

issues.title: Delivered sensitivity differs markedly from the profile value and is strongly glucose dependent
issues.detail: The profile declares a single flat sensitivity of 56 mg/dL/U, but the loop applied 124.0, 111.9 and 108.4 mg/dL/U at glucose of 69.8, 95.1 and 84 mg/dL, and 42.5, 43.2, 39.99, 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U at glucose from 135 to 246 mg/dL. The delivered response is therefore roughly half as strong as the profile value in the normal range and roughly twice as strong at high glucose, which matches the observed slow climb followed by an abrupt fall.

issues.title: Unannounced-meal microbolus cap exceeds the standard cap while carbohydrates are never announced
issues.detail: The maximum unannounced-meal microbolus is set to 20 basal minutes against a standard maximum of 15 basal minutes. Because carbohydrate entries are zero, the larger and more speculative cap is the only one that ever applies. The variant additionally delivered above the standard bolus cap in documented cycles, microbolusing 0.4 U against a standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U on 08-07 and delivering 1.6 U under a high boost on 08-19.

issues.title: Effective target deviates from the declared target schedule
issues.detail: The profile declares targets of 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL, but loop statuses show effective targets of 80, 84, 86, 87, 96.4, 99, 101, 104, 105, 106, 108 and 116 mg/dL, including values below the declared floor when no temporary target was active. Autosens is disabled and both Autosens target adjustment flags are false, so those settings do not explain it. This appears to be intentional variant behaviour, but it means no target change can be validated from this package.

issues.title: No carbohydrate data at all, which blocks several assessments
issues.detail: Carbohydrate entries, total grams and extended carbohydrate entries are all zero, carb_treatment_entries is empty and carbohydrates on board were zero in every supplied loop status. As a result the five carb ratio segments were never exercised, the carbohydrate absorption model settings were inert throughout, and unannounced-meal detection is the entire meal response, which fixes it as reactive by construction.

issues.title: Multiple confounders on the worst days
issues.detail: The two poorest days are 08-14 with 70.8 percent time in range and 08-18 with 12.8 percent time below range, both adjacent to GLP-1 1.25 mg doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20. Infusion site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, a profile switch on 08-13, and a recorded occlusion with pump error on 08-19 further limit attribution of any single day to a profile setting.

recommendations.title: Primary: discuss tightening the maximum insulin on board ceiling first, as a behaviourally neutral safety bound
recommendations.description: This is the only supported action that addresses the dominant safety finding without depending on any unresolved competition between basal, sensitivity, detection lag and meal effects. The configured limit of 25 U exceeds a full day of total insulin use, given 275.95 U logged over fourteen days against a 16.2 U per day scheduled basal. Nothing in fourteen days approached even 8 U, with observed peaks of 5.935 U at 245 mg/dL and 4.73 U at 262 mg/dL, both with zero carbohydrates on board. A ceiling well below 25 U would therefore leave every routine dosing decision in the observed period untouched while bounding exactly the accumulation that preceded the documented falls of 234 to 56 mg/dL within 120 minutes on 08-14, 264 to 96 within 120 minutes on 08-19 and 206 to 53 within 180 minutes on 08-16. Because it does not alter normal behaviour, it also creates a clean baseline for evaluating any later change. The specific value belongs to the care team and should reflect the individual maximum meal bolus plus basal accumulation.

suggested_change.review_range: a value materially below 25 U, discussed with the care team, chosen so that no dosing observed in this period would have been blocked
suggested_change.expected_effect: truncates worst-case accumulation without changing routine dosing
monitor: peak insulin on board with zero carbohydrates on board

recommendations.title: Consider aligning the configured maximum basal with the ceiling the loop already applies
recommendations.description: The configured 12 U/h is roughly fifteen times the highest scheduled basal of 0.8 U/h and was never the binding constraint. The loop text on 08-14 shows an adjusted requested rate of 5.9 U/h limited to a maximum safe basal of 4 U/h, consistent with the daily safety multiplier of 5 applied to the peak basal. Bringing the configured value near the already effective 4 U/h would be behaviourally neutral for this dataset while restoring a meaningful bound. This changes the safe action order only in the sense that it belongs in the same ceiling-first stage as the primary recommendation, but it should still be introduced as a separate step so that each change remains attributable.

suggested_change.review_range: near the effective maximum safe basal of 4 U/h already applied by the loop
suggested_change.expected_effect: no change to observed behaviour; restores a meaningful upper bound
monitor: frequency of temporary basal requests reaching the ceiling

recommendations.title: Defer the unannounced-meal microbolus cap to a separate later round
recommendations.description: The maximum unannounced-meal microbolus of 20 basal minutes exceeds the standard 15 basal minutes, and because carbohydrates are never announced it is the only cap that ever applies, which points the wrong way given 15.3 percent time below range at 19:00 local. This is a genuine candidate, but it changes routine delivery rather than only the worst case, and its effect size is uncertain because the variant delivered 0.4 U against a standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U on 08-07 and 1.6 U under a high boost on 08-19. It should therefore follow the ceiling changes rather than accompany them, so that any change in evening lows can be attributed.

suggested_change.review_range: consider aligning towards the standard 15 minutes only after the ceiling changes have been observed
suggested_change.expected_effect: smaller speculative microboluses during unannounced rises; effect may be limited by boost behaviour
monitor: time below range at 18:00 to 20:00 local

recommendations.title: Start logging carbohydrates for one recurring meal before any nutrition-related setting is considered
recommendations.description: With zero carbohydrate entries, the five carb ratio segments were never exercised, the carbohydrate absorption settings were inert, and unannounced-meal detection is the entire meal response. Logging the afternoon meal that precedes the 16:00 local peak of 162.8 mg/dL would convert carb ratio, the absorption model and the detection lag from untestable into testable, and would separate detection lag from the afternoon basal trough and from temporary-target microbolus suppression. Logging rescue carbohydrate taken during lows matters equally, because the rebounds of 80 to 157 mg/dL after level 2 lows indicate carbohydrate that the system currently re-detects as a new unannounced rise. This changes the safe action order because it is the prerequisite for every meal-related assessment in a future review.

suggested_change.review_range: log amount and time for one recurring afternoon meal for 7 to 10 days, plus rescue carbohydrate during lows
suggested_change.expected_effect: no change to insulin settings; enables evaluation of carb ratio and the absorption model
monitor: carbohydrates on board appearing in loop status
time below range at 18:00 to 20:00 local

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all seven basal segments, all five carb ratio segments, the flat sensitivity of 56 mg/dL/U, all three targets and the 10 hour duration of insulin action unchanged in this round, and instead verify the afternoon window by logging the meal that precedes the 16:00 local peak for 7 to 10 consecutive days while every insulin setting stays fixed.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The evidence does not yet separate a profile defect from automation behaviour and unannounced meals. The most fasting-like window, 04:00 to 08:00 local, achieves 95 to 98 percent time in range with only 1.3 to 4.8 percent below range under the current 0.6 to 0.8 U/h, which argues against a general basal error. The apparent phase mismatch, where basal is lowest at 0.5 U/h from 16:00 exactly at the 162.8 mg/dL peak and steps up at 18:00 and 19:00 into the hours with the highest low burden, is real on paper but has at least four unresolved explanations: detection lag with zero announced carbohydrates, GLP-1 delayed absorption on a three-day dosing cadence, microbolus suppression during the recurring 135 mg/dL temporary targets, and infusion set effects including the recorded occlusion on 08-19. Carb ratio cannot be assessed because it was never exercised. The flat sensitivity value cannot be assessed in isolation because the delivered sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U under the dynamic path, so editing 56 mg/dL/U would move the entire curve and confound the dynamic factor. Targets cannot be assessed because the effective target ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL rather than the declared 90, 100 and 90. Duration of insulin action at 10 hours is plausibly implicated in the long correction tails, such as 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL preceding 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes on 08-17, but it is coupled to the sensitivity and ceiling settings and must not be changed alongside them. Raising afternoon insulin exposure now would also conflict with the dominant safety constraint, because that insulin tail lands in the 18:00 to 20:00 window where time below range reaches 15.3 percent.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Log the carbohydrate amount and exact time of the single meal preceding the 14:00 to 17:00 local plateau every day for 7 to 10 days with no other change, then re-examine whether the 16:00 local average of 162.8 mg/dL falls once the rise is announced rather than detected; if it does not fall, the afternoon basal segments become the next candidate, and if it does, detection lag was the cause and no basal change is warranted.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local hours 00:00 to 03:00 show averages of 90.6 to 106 mg/dL with time below range of 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent, but the decline begins in the evening at 22:00 with 127.6 mg/dL falling through 105.7 at 23:00 and self-corrects from 04:00 under the same 0.6 U/h rate. Uncertainty: a basal that was genuinely excessive would not self-correct while the rate is unchanged, so the residual insulin tail from evening corrections is the better-supported explanation, supported by 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL preceding 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes on 08-17. Dependencies: coupled to the 10 hour duration of insulin action, to the dynamic sensitivity curve and to the pending insulin on board ceiling change, which must be observed first.

Evidence: 05:00 local shows an average of 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent time in range and 4.8 percent below range, one of the best hours in the period. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment; the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 08-21 is isolated and coincides with a sensor change the same morning. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; this segment anchors the conclusion that overall basal magnitude is reasonable.

Evidence: hours 06:00 to 08:00 local show averages of 99.5, 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL with 97.5, 98.7 and 98.2 percent time in range and 0 to 2.5 percent below range under the highest scheduled rate in the profile. Uncertainty: low; this is the strongest-performing window in the dataset. Dependencies: none; no change is supportable against this performance.

Evidence: the rise begins here, with 10:00 local at 148.0 mg/dL and 20.2 percent above range, and 08:00 immediately before shows 0 percent below range and only 1.8 percent above range. Uncertainty: high, because the meal-shaped onset with zero announced carbohydrates makes detection lag at least as plausible as a basal deficit, and GLP-1 dosing on a three-day cadence may shift absorption. Dependencies: cannot be separated from unannounced-meal detection behaviour until one recurring meal is logged; raising this segment would also add insulin whose tail lands in the 18:00 to 20:00 low window.

Evidence: this is the lowest scheduled rate and it coincides with the daily peak of 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 local with 32.1 percent above range and 0.0 percent below range, which superficially suggests under-dosing. Uncertainty: high, because four explanations remain unseparated, namely detection lag with zero announced carbohydrates, GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying, microbolus suppression during the 135 mg/dL temporary targets recorded on 08-17, 08-18 and 08-19, and infusion set effects including the 08-19 occlusion. Dependencies: any increase here delivers insulin whose action peaks in the 18:00 to 20:00 window, where time below range is 7.7 and 15.3 percent with two level 2 events; this must not be changed before the meal logging check and the ceiling changes.

Evidence: 18:00 local shows 124.2 mg/dL with 7.7 percent below range, and the segment steps up into the worst daytime low hour. Uncertainty: the lows here follow documented large falls such as 234 to 56 mg/dL within 120 minutes on 08-14 and 206 to 53 within 180 minutes on 08-16, so the correction tail is better supported than the basal step as the cause. Dependencies: attribution requires observing the effect of the insulin on board ceiling change first; changing basal and a ceiling together would make the outcome uninterpretable.

Evidence: 19:00 local carries the highest daytime low burden at 15.3 percent below range with an average of 105.4 mg/dL and includes the level 2 cluster of 48, 41 and 41 mg/dL on 08-14. Uncertainty: this is the strongest candidate for a future basal reduction, but the same hour is reached by the tail of afternoon corrections, and the 08-14 event followed a 0.2 U correction at 234 mg/dL, so the driver is not yet isolated. Dependencies: must wait until the insulin on board ceiling and, if needed, the unannounced-meal microbolus cap have been observed; reducing basal first would risk masking the actual cause and could worsen the afternoon elevation.

Evidence: carbohydrate entries are zero, total carbohydrates are 0.0 g, carb_treatment_entries is empty and carbohydrates on board were zero in every supplied loop status, so this ratio was never used to compute a bolus. Uncertainty: total for the value itself; the segment is confirmed loaded because the profile ratios are echoed in loop reason strings. Dependencies: becomes assessable only after carbohydrates are logged for recurring meals; keep rather than change because the current value exists and no change is supportable.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entry exists in the fourteen-day window, so this segment produced no observable dosing. Uncertainty: total; the 04:00 to 08:00 window is the best-performing period of the day but that reflects basal and fasting behaviour, not carbohydrate ratio performance. Dependencies: requires announced meals before any evaluation is possible.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries mean this segment was never exercised, even though the morning rise from 110.5 mg/dL at 08:00 to 148.0 at 10:00 falls inside it. Uncertainty: total for the ratio; the rise is attributable to unannounced-meal detection lag rather than to a carbohydrate ratio that was never applied. Dependencies: assessable only with logged morning carbohydrates.

Evidence: this is the tightest ratio in the profile and it covers the highest above-range hours, 16:00 at 32.1 percent and 17:00 at 22.6 percent, yet zero carbohydrate entries mean it never generated a bolus. Uncertainty: total; no inference about its correctness can be drawn from the afternoon elevation, which is a detection and automation pattern rather than a carbohydrate ratio outcome. Dependencies: this is the priority segment for the recommended single-meal logging check.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries; the evening lows in this window followed small corrections and their tails, not meal boluses, as shown by 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL on 08-17 preceding 68 mg/dL at 180 minutes and 57 at 240 minutes. Uncertainty: total for the ratio value. Dependencies: unlogged rescue carbohydrate in this window is a confounder that must be recorded before any evaluation.

Evidence: the declared flat value is not what is delivered, because dynamic sensitivity is enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor and the applied sensitivity ranged from 124.0, 111.9 and 108.4 mg/dL/U at glucose of 69.8, 95.1 and 84 mg/dL down to 42.5, 43.2, 39.99, 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U at glucose from 135 to 246 mg/dL. Uncertainty: high, because this profile value acts as a scaling reference for the whole dynamic curve rather than as the direct correction factor, so a change would move both the weak normal-range response and the strong high-glucose response at once. Dependencies: tightly coupled to the dynamic sensitivity adjustment factor and to the boost behaviour; only one of these may be reopened later, and only if the low burden persists after the ceiling changes.

Evidence: the declared value is 90 mg/dL, but loop statuses show effective targets of 80, 84, 86, 87, 96.4 and higher, including values below the declared floor when no temporary target was recorded. Uncertainty: high, because Autosens is disabled and both Autosens target adjustment flags are false, so the deviation is not explained by any inventory setting and appears to be intentional variant behaviour. Dependencies: no target change can be validated from this package; the mechanism should be clarified with the care team before any target edit is considered.

Evidence: the declared daytime target of 100 mg/dL is conservative and appropriate given time below range of 5.1 percent, yet observed effective targets during daytime cycles included 80 mg/dL at 262 and 245 mg/dL and 116 mg/dL on a hypo-guard cycle. Uncertainty: high, because the delivered target is dynamically modulated in a risk-inverse direction that the declared schedule does not describe. Dependencies: raising the declared target might reduce afternoon dosing pressure, but with the effective target already overridden the outcome would be unpredictable, so no change is supportable.

Evidence: this segment covers the start of the late-evening decline, where 23:00 local averages 105.7 mg/dL with 10.1 percent below range. Uncertainty: high, because the observed lows in this window follow evening correction tails rather than target-driven dosing, and the effective target deviates from the declared value. Dependencies: any target discussion must follow clarification of the dynamic target mechanism and must not coincide with the ceiling or basal work.

Evidence: a 10 hour duration with a free peak insulin model is consistent with the observed long tails, where 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL preceded 68 mg/dL at 180 minutes and 57 at 240 minutes on 08-17, 0.15 U at 138 preceded 82 to 87 mg/dL on 08-12, and 0.05 U at 93 preceded 69 mg/dL on 08-10, since such small boluses cannot themselves cause those falls. Uncertainty: high, because no insulin on board time series was supplied to test the decay curve directly, and 10 hours may be the intended setting for this insulin model rather than an error. Dependencies: the duration interacts with the dynamic sensitivity curve and with the insulin on board ceiling; changing it alongside either would make attribution impossible, so it is held until the ceiling change has been observed.

Evidence: both components are non-null and enabled, and with zero carbohydrate entries and carbohydrates on board zero in all supplied statuses, unannounced-meal detection is the entire meal-response system; disabling either would remove the only meal response. Uncertainty: the arrangement is reactive by construction, which sets a floor on afternoon time above range, but that is a strategy consequence rather than a misconfiguration, and unannounced-meal detection is not duplicating carbohydrate counting here. Dependencies: the reactive lag is best addressed by logging carbohydrates, not by disabling these switches; verify is not available because no component is null.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, smb_with_temp_target_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: always-enabled microbolusing supersedes the with-carbohydrates and after-carbohydrates switches, so those two are inert labels rather than active restrictions, which is a cosmetic inconsistency only. The materially active condition is that microbolusing is disabled during high temporary targets, which suppressed dosing during the 135 mg/dL temporary targets on 08-17, 08-18 and 08-19, all overlapping the highest above-range afternoon hours. Uncertainty: that suppression plausibly contributes to afternoon time above range on those specific days, but it is hypo-protective and the user appears to apply those targets deliberately, with no activity log available to confirm the reason. Dependencies: enabling microbolusing during high temporary targets would push against the dominant safety constraint of 5.1 percent time below range with two level 2 evening events, so no change is supportable; verify is not available because all five components are non-null.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB strength and frequency (smb_interval_minutes, max_smb_basal_minutes, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes)
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: the unannounced-meal cap of 20 basal minutes exceeds the standard 15 basal minutes, and since carbohydrates are never announced the larger speculative cap is the only one that applies, which points the wrong way against 15.3 percent time below range at 19:00 local. The 3 minute interval is not the binding rate limiter because CGM cadence is 5.0 minutes and loop cycles follow the CGM. Uncertainty: high on effect size, because the variant delivered above the configured standard bolus cap in documented cycles, microbolusing 0.4 U against a standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U on 08-07 and 1.6 U under a high boost on 08-19, so tightening the cap may achieve less than the setting implies. Dependencies: this changes routine delivery, unlike the ceilings, so it is deliberately deferred to a later separate round after the insulin on board ceiling has been observed; keep now rather than change so that no two dependent delivery settings move together.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: both ceilings are inert. The loop capped an adjusted request of 5.9 U/h at a maximum safe basal of 4 U/h on 08-14, so 12 U/h never bound anything and 4 U/h reproduces the ceiling already in force. The 25 U insulin on board limit exceeds a full day of insulin, given 275.95 U over fourteen days and a 16.2 U per day scheduled basal, while the highest observed insulin on board was 5.935 U at 245 mg/dL and 4.73 U at 262 mg/dL, both with zero carbohydrates on board; a limit of 8 U would therefore not have blocked any dosing observed in this period while bounding the accumulation that preceded 234 to 56 mg/dL within 120 minutes on 08-14, 264 to 96 within 120 minutes on 08-19 and 206 to 53 within 180 minutes on 08-16. Uncertainty: the suggested values are candidates for care-team review, not prescriptions, and the appropriate insulin on board ceiling depends on the individual largest meal bolus plus basal accumulation, which cannot be derived here because no meal boluses exist in the data. Dependencies: none blocking, which is precisely why this is sequenced first; it is behaviourally neutral for the observed period and therefore creates a clean baseline before any delivery or profile change. The two components should still be introduced one at a time.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / Autosens and Dynamic ISF (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, autosens_raises_target, autosens_lowers_target, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: the configuration is internally coherent, with one sensitivity path rather than two, and with Autosens off the target adjustment flags are correctly inert. A sensitivity ratio of 1 in most statuses is a neutral current adjustment and not evidence of anything disabled; the values 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 occur on hypo-guard cycles and are consistent with the dynamic path working. The delivered sensitivity nevertheless spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U, roughly twice as strong as the profile value at high glucose and about half as strong in the normal range, which matches the observed slow climb and abrupt fall. Uncertainty: high and bidirectional, because lowering the adjustment factor would reduce the high-glucose over-correction and help the 5.1 percent time below range but would simultaneously weaken the already slow 100 to 150 mg/dL response and worsen the 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 local. Dependencies: coupled to the flat profile sensitivity of 56 mg/dL/U and to the boost behaviour, so three inputs feed one outcome; this may be reopened only after the ceiling change has been observed, and then only instead of, never together with, a profile sensitivity change. Verify is not available because all five components are non-null.

Evidence: both values are present and conventional, and both were inert for the entire period because carbohydrate entries are zero, extended carbohydrate entries are zero, carb_treatment_entries is empty and carbohydrates on board were zero in every supplied loop status, so neither parameter influenced a single dosing decision. Uncertainty: no observational basis exists to tune either value, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate, since the average extended carbohydrate duration field is null. Dependencies: relevance is blocked by the absence of carbohydrate logging rather than by any data-quality defect; this group becomes assessable only once meals are announced, so keep is used rather than change or verify, and verify is unavailable because both components are non-null.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Before setting any prebolus interval, immediate bolus percentage or extended carbohydrate configuration, begin announcing carbohydrates for recurring meals, starting with the single meal that precedes the 14:00 to 17:00 local plateau, and log rescue carbohydrate taken during lows. Keep microbolusing and unannounced-meal detection enabled throughout, since they are currently the entire meal response and must not be removed; because always-enabled microbolusing is active, announcing carbohydrates adds information without switching on a second dosing pathway. Do not introduce a prebolus interval, an immediate bolus split or extended carbohydrates in the same round as any insulin setting change, because with delivered sensitivity reaching 27.8 mg/dL/U at high glucose, a 10 hour duration of insulin action and an insulin on board ceiling of 25 U still in place, adding announced insulin on top of existing boost behaviour would increase rather than reduce the evening low risk that currently stands at 5.1 percent time below range with two level 2 events.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user-declared analysis context is present with source declared_by_user and a declaration timestamp of 2026-08-21T21:08:10Z, and within it meal_strategies is an empty list, period_exceptions is null and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so there is no declared prebolus, immediate bolus percentage or extended carbohydrate value to compare against execution and no representative period-wide declaration can be assumed. Declared context and telemetry agree rather than conflict, since an empty declaration matches zero logged carbohydrates. All 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses with the extended carbohydrate flag false, and they show a repeating cycle of unannounced rise, late correction, level 2 low and rebound: 0.2 U at 100 mg/dL rising to 235 at 240 minutes on 08-14; 0.2 U at 172 falling to 47 at 240 minutes then rebounding to 204 at 360 minutes on 08-13; 0.25 U at 206 falling to 53 at 180 minutes then 158 at 240 minutes on 08-16. Rebounds of 80 to 157 mg/dL within 60 to 120 minutes of a level 2 low cannot arise from insulin dynamics, indicating rescue carbohydrate that is not logged and is therefore re-detected as a new unannounced rise. Announcement is the only intervention that breaks this cycle at its first link rather than its last, and it is also the prerequisite for evaluating the five carb ratio segments and the carbohydrate absorption model, both of which are currently untestable.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log the carbohydrate amount and exact eating time for the single meal preceding the 14:00 to 17:00 local plateau every day for 7 to 10 days, with no other setting changed and no prebolus added, then check whether carbohydrates on board appear in loop status and whether the 16:00 local average of 162.8 mg/dL and its 32.1 percent above range decrease.

exceptions.pattern: The 14:00 to 17:00 local plateau, where averages run 148.1, 153.0, 162.8 and 148.9 mg/dL with above range of 26.3, 23.6, 32.1 and 22.6 percent and 0.0 percent below range at 16:00, immediately followed by the worst low window at 18:00 and 19:00 with 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range.
exceptions.suggestion: Make this the first and only meal to announce, and observe it for 7 to 10 days before any other meal or setting is touched.
exceptions.rationale: It carries the largest share of above-range time and it precedes the evening lows, and three explanations still overlap here, namely detection lag, the 0.5 U/h basal trough from 16:00 and microbolus suppression during the 135 mg/dL temporary targets recorded on 08-17, 08-18 and 08-19; announcing this one meal separates them without changing any insulin setting.

exceptions.pattern: Post-hypoglycaemia rebounds, with 47 to 204 mg/dL within about two hours on 08-13, 53 to 158 mg/dL on 08-16 and 41 to 136 mg/dL on 08-14, all following documented level 2 lows.
exceptions.suggestion: Record rescue carbohydrate as a carbohydrate entry at the time it is taken, and treat the resulting rebound as already treated rather than as a new correction target.
exceptions.rationale: Unlogged rescue carbohydrate is currently indistinguishable from a new meal, so the system re-doses into a rebound that is already resolving, which feeds the next cycle; note that the minimum carbohydrate requirement of 20 g means small rescue amounts may not trigger carbohydrate-dependent logic, so the value here is visibility rather than dosing.

implementation_steps: Step 0, before any change: share this analysis with the diabetes care team and agree which items may be trialled, since every item below is decision support only and requires independent verification.

Step 1, data and profile stage, no insulin change: keep all seventeen profile parameters exactly as they are and start logging carbohydrates for the single recurring meal that precedes the 14:00 to 17:00 local plateau, plus any rescue carbohydrate taken during lows, for 7 to 10 days. Record whether carbohydrates on board begin appearing in loop status.

Step 2, automation stage, first ceiling: after care-team agreement, discuss reducing the maximum insulin on board from 25 U to a value that would not have blocked any dosing observed in this period, with 8 U as the candidate given the 5.935 U peak. Change this one setting alone and observe for at least 14 days, tracking time below range at 19:00 local and between 23:00 and 03:00 local, and the peak insulin on board when carbohydrates on board are zero.

Step 3, automation stage, second ceiling: only after step 2 has been observed, discuss aligning the maximum basal from 12 U/h to about 4 U/h, matching the maximum safe basal the loop already applies. Expect no behavioural change; if behaviour does change, revert and re-evaluate before proceeding.

Step 4, automation stage, delivery limit: only if evening lows persist after steps 2 and 3, discuss aligning the maximum unannounced-meal microbolus from 20 basal minutes towards the 15 basal minutes standard cap. Change this alone and observe for 14 days, noting that boost behaviour may limit the effect.

Step 5, reassessment: re-run the analysis with the meal-logging data from step 1 and the observation periods from steps 2 to 4, then evaluate whether the afternoon elevation persists once meals are announced.

Step 6, only if the low burden still persists after all the above: reopen exactly one of the dynamic sensitivity adjustment factor of 70 percent or the flat profile sensitivity of 56 mg/dL/U, never both, and never together with a basal or duration of insulin action change.

Step 7, deferred pending clarification: ask the care team or the AAPS variant documentation to explain why the effective target ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL against a declared schedule of 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL, and why microboluses of 0.4 U and 1.6 U exceeded the standard bolus cap; do not adjust targets until this is understood.

Throughout: change one setting at a time, allow at least 7 to 14 days of observation between changes, avoid drawing conclusions from days containing an infusion set change, a sensor change, a GLP-1 dose or a pump error, and stop and consult the care team immediately if severe lows occur.
education: Time below range is the metric that most constrains what can safely be changed. At 5.1 percent overall this exceeds the commonly used 4 percent target, and because it is clustered at specific local hours rather than spread evenly, it points to a repeating mechanism at those times rather than to a general excess of insulin.

When dynamic sensitivity is enabled, the sensitivity value in the profile stops being the correction factor that is actually applied and becomes a scaling reference for a glucose-dependent curve. In this dataset the applied value ranged from about 124 mg/dL/U at low glucose to about 27.8 mg/dL/U at high glucose against a profile value of 56, which is why comparing outcomes directly against the profile number can be misleading.

A ceiling setting such as maximum insulin on board or maximum basal only affects behaviour when the system actually reaches it. Ceilings far above observed usage are effectively inert, which makes lowering them towards realistic values an unusually low-risk change, because it alters nothing in normal operation while still bounding the worst case.

A rapid rise shortly after a low that insulin cannot explain usually indicates carbohydrate that the system cannot see. Logging rescue carbohydrate matters as much as logging meals, because an unlogged recovery looks to the algorithm like a brand-new unexplained rise and can trigger a further correction into an excursion that is already resolving.

A long duration of insulin action means small doses keep acting for many hours. That is why a very small correction can be followed by a large fall several hours later: the fall mostly reflects insulin given earlier, not the small dose itself.

When several settings could each produce the same glucose pattern, changing more than one at a time makes the result impossible to interpret. Sequential single changes with a defined observation window are slower but are the only way to learn which setting was responsible.

Days containing an infusion set change, a sensor change, a medication dose that affects gastric emptying, or a recorded pump error should be treated as confounded and excluded from conclusions about profile settings.

Extended carbohydrate entries are a carbohydrate-modelling feature and are not the same thing as a pump extended bolus; their absence here means the carbohydrate absorption model was never exercised, which is different from a statement about how insulin was delivered.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and is not medical advice. Every proposed change must be independently verified with your diabetes care team before it is applied.
Nothing here should be applied automatically to AAPS. Make changes manually, one at a time, and monitor glucose closely after each change.

The most important safety finding is the clustered hypoglycaemia at 19:00 local and between 23:00 and 03:00 local, together with three documented level 2 lows at 42, 41 and 42 mg/dL. Discuss this pattern with your care team before making any change that could increase insulin exposure in the afternoon or evening.

At the end of the analysed period the system was at 245 mg/dL and rising with 5.935 U of insulin on board and no carbohydrates on board, with a 4 U/h temporary basal requested. This is the same precondition that preceded the documented rapid falls, and it warrants close monitoring and care-team discussion.

No change to basal, carb ratio, insulin sensitivity, target or duration of insulin action is supported by this dataset. The apparent afternoon basal mismatch has several unresolved explanations and must not be treated as a confirmed profile defect.

The suggested ceiling values are candidates for discussion, not prescriptions. The appropriate maximum insulin on board depends on your individual largest meal bolus plus basal accumulation, which cannot be derived from this package because no meal boluses were recorded.

The maximum daily safety multiplier of 5.0 and the current basal safety multiplier of 6.0 both exceed common defaults and together widen the safety envelope; these are outside the reviewed decision groups and should be raised with your care team.
